_doc.what: Decision & node registry (FOC-448) — one typed place per model-made judgment and per v2 graph-node step. Graph-node entries carry the ADR-0012 D7 contract copied verbatim from docs/plans/graph-json-v2-design.md §3.1–§3.9 (a config/graph.json v2 step object stays exactly-D7 and copies reads/output/tier/failure/writes from here); transport entries carry the question set their call-site sends to the decision-call seam.
_doc.consumers: scripts/decision-registry.mjs (loader: validates every entry, lookup by id, question resolution + template instantiation), scripts/decision-call.mjs (decisionId lookups + the A0 annotation rule + runner-built-question governance), scripts/mcp/steps.mjs (FOC-401 question templates), scripts/graph-runner.mjs (FOC-397: [J] steps and decide edges by registry id).
_doc.autonomy: A0 = the entry produces a model-made judgment whose A0-ENFORCED channel (the decision-call seam decisionId path) serves it as an annotation only — no caller field can request action semantics. Seed A0 entries: gate.screen (supervisor-fixed), extraction, prompt-refinement, plan.dor, plan.decompose, the ten FOC-452 PLAN gate entries, and the six decide-edge entries (intake.triage_node, intake.has_acceptance_criteria, intake.task_size, review.depth, orchestration.next_step, monitor.child_state). Start posture, stated honestly: nothing calibrated (thresholds null; FOC-387 has not run); the runner (FOC-397) serves plan.dor/plan.decompose and the decide edges through the seam's A0-enforced decisionId channel; extraction and prompt-refinement are served by the built FOC-401 step servers routed through the seam's inline channel since FOC-397 — their code programmatically acts on answers inside the tool boundary, that built boundary is declared per path in the serving field and is gated to FOC-387. null = not an autonomy-managed decision, and the encoding is structural: autonomy is null IFF kind is one of G, A, H, D (node configs — the [G] generator node per the roadmap note, the [A] agent node gated by plan.gate1, the [H] human gates, the [D] deterministic node — are step configuration, not decisions), while kind J requires autonomy in {A0, A1, A2} (AC1's autonomy list binds decision entries). A1/A2 are evidence-backed promotions granted by Mateusz (FOC-387 calibration), never self-granted.
_doc.serving: Machine-readable serving scope, required and NON-EMPTY on kind-J entries (FOC-397: an entry nothing serves must not sit in the registry, and every path that serves it in code must appear here). One record per serving path: via = the channel; actsOnAnswers = this path, as built today, programmatically consumes answers into operative output; a0Enforced = this path returns the A0 annotation-only shape, loader-enforced (true only on the seam decisionId channel); gate = the FOC that owns bringing the path under A0 governance — REQUIRED whenever actsOnAnswers=true && a0Enforced=false. Schema cross-rules: kind J ⇒ serving present and non-empty; kind != J ⇒ serving forbidden; a0Enforced ⇒ via is the seam; via "seam" ⇒ a0Enforced (the name is reserved for the enforced decisionId channel — the seam's inline channel is "seam (inline)"); a0Enforced ⇒ autonomy A0; autonomy A0 ⇒ every declared path is a0Enforced or names a gate.
_doc.threshold: null in every seed entry — FOC-387 writes calibration rows; never invent numbers.
_doc.fallback: tier2 is "disabled" in every entry while scripts/decision-call.mjs FALLBACK_MODEL is null (FOC-473): a tier-1 failure goes fail-closed to the relay/HITL path, or escalates where the entry's D7 failure field says so. Tier-2 is never claimed live; the registry test enforces the correspondence with the shipped constant.
_doc.criteriaVersion: Bumped when an entry's question text changes; recorded on every registry-sourced call (envelope, shadow JSONL line, meter event).
_doc.outOfScope: egress.contains_secret and test.failure.cause are NOT entries here — they enter when their owners land (FOC-391 egress wiring; the TEST failure-cause owner). The five decide-edge ids (intake.triage_node, intake.task_size, review.depth, orchestration.next_step, monitor.child_state) landed with FOC-397; intake.has_acceptance_criteria joined them with FOC-451.

The decide-edge entries: config/graph.json decisionEdges (FOC-397; intake.has_acceptance_criteria FOC-451); question text designed from the MAP descriptions (FOC-452), the built prompt-refinement analogue and the DoR rubric.

plan.dod.prompt: You generate the Definition of Done for one planning inbox entry. Work only from the declared inputs you are given — the issue title and the accepted scope summary the inbox entry carries; no repo tree, no telemetry, no prior runs, no Linear comments, and never the sibling generator's feature list (context size is a design output). Make exactly one model call with no tool loop. The DoD derives from the issue's own accepted scope: every item is a verifiable, bounded check on what THIS issue delivers — no invented scope, no feature the issue does not name, no estimates or counts. Use the repo's DoD conventions: a bounded checklist of 1 to 12 items, each item one verifiable statement of at most 200 characters, classified with kind — test (a named test or the suite that must pass), lint (the linter or a static check that must exit clean), manual (a human verification step) or linear (a Linear-side fact: labels, state transition, hand-off comment); set bounded true only when the check is machine-checkable as written. Recurring repo conventions are legitimate DoD substance where the scope implies them: the test suite green, lint exit 0, the docs state file updated, one commit carrying the issue id. Your output must validate against this entry's output schema — one object {definitionOfDone} whose items are {check, kind, bounded} — before anything downstream sees it; a schema-invalid or failed call stops the step fail-closed with one typed failure record, never partial data. Runs on the cheap tier.

plan.ac.prompt: You generate acceptance criteria for one planning inbox entry. Work only from the declared inputs — the dictated issue text (title, scope summary, any Definition-of-Ready facts) and the extracted candidate files; no repo tree, no telemetry, no prior runs, no Linear comments, and never the sibling generator's Definition of Done (context size is a design output). Make exactly one model call with no tool loop, no tools and no repo access. Derive the criteria from the issue's own accepted scope: one criterion per observable behaviour the issue names — no invented scope, no feature the issue does not name, and never count, size or compute anything (sizes, counts and estimates belong to plan.decompose plus the code-side mapping). Use the repo's AC conventions: a bounded list of 1 to 12 items; each item an object {id, text, kind, evidence} where id matches ^AC-[0-9]{1,2}$, text is one declarative statement within 300 characters, kind is behaviour (an observable outcome of correct behaviour), boundary (a limit, refusal or error path) or verification (how the delivered work is checked), and evidence names what would demonstrate the criterion — test (a named test or the suite), command_output (a command's observable output), file_state (a file's content or existence) or human_check (a human verification step). Evidence typing discipline: pick the evidence type a reviewer could actually check as written; a criterion nobody could check as written is a defect, not a style choice. Your output must validate against this entry's output schema before anything downstream sees it; a schema-invalid or failed call stops the step fail-closed with one typed failure record — never partial data. Runs on the cheap tier.
